docs.title: PepData
docs.text: Look up shipped amino-acid properties and pairwise matrices, encode peptide sequences, or load peptide assay tables from IEDB. Property lookups work offline; IEDB acquisition requires a download and has separate assay filters.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
python -m pip install pepdata

Python 3.9 or later is required.

docs.title: Look up a peptide's residue properties
docs.text:
from pepdata.amino_acid_properties import hydropathy

peptide = "ACD"
print([hydropathy[residue] for residue in peptide])

[1.8, 2.5, -3.5]

The values come from the shipped residue-property table. The dictionary maps single-letter residues to numeric values; it does not predict MHC binding or clinical immunogenicity. Use uppercase canonical residue letters. A missing letter raises KeyError.

docs.title: Find the interface you need
docs.text:
Task Module or object Single-residue properties pepdata.amino_acid_properties BLOSUM substitution matrices pepdata.blosum PMBEC and contact tables pepdata.pmbec, pepdata.residue_contact_energies Residue alphabets pepdata.amino_acid_alphabet, pepdata.reduced_alphabet N-gram features pepdata.PeptideVectorizer MHC-binding assay tables pepdata.iedb.mhc T-cell assay tables pepdata.iedb.tcell

The property dictionaries are in amino_acid_properties, rather than amino_acid. There is no StringTransformer interface in this package.

See residue and pairwise tables, then peptide features and IEDB tables. The API reference follows those same tasks.

docs.title: read_pmbec_coefficients
docs.text:
read_pmbec_coefficients(key_type='row', verbose=True, filename=join(MATRIX_DIR, 'pmbec.mat'))

Parameters:

  • filename (str, default: join(MATRIX_DIR, 'pmbec.mat') ) –

    Location of PMBEC coefficient matrix

  • key_type (str, default: 'row' ) –

    'row' : every key is a single amino acid, which maps to a dictionary for that row 'pair' : every key is a tuple of amino acids 'pair_string' : every key is a string of two amino acid characters

  • verbose (bool, default: True ) –

    Print rows of matrix as we read them

docs.title: load_dataframe
docs.text:
load_dataframe(mhc_class=None, hla=None, exclude_hla=None, human_only=False, peptide_length=None, assay_method=None, only_standard_amino_acids=True, warn_bad_lines=True, nrows=None)

Load IEDB MHC data without aggregating multiple entries for the same epitope

Parameters:

  • mhc_class (int | None, default: None ) –

    Restrict to MHC Class I or Class II (or None for neither)

  • hla (str | None, default: None ) –

    Restrict results to specific HLA type used in assay (regex pattern)

  • exclude_hla (str | None, default: None ) –

    Regex pattern to exclude certain HLA types

  • human_only (bool, default: False ) –

    Restrict to human samples (default False)

  • peptide_length (int | None, default: None ) –

    Restrict epitopes to amino acid strings of given length

  • assay_method (str | None, default: None ) –

    Limit to assay methods which contain the given string

  • only_standard_amino_acids (bool, default: True ) –

    Drop sequences which use non-standard amino acids, anything outside the core 20, such as X or U (default = True)

  • warn_bad_lines (bool, default: True ) –

    The full MHC ligand dataset seems to contain several dozen lines with too many fields. This currently results in a lot of warning messages from Pandas, which you can turn off with this option (default = True)

  • nrows (int | None, default: None ) –

    Don't load the full IEDB dataset but instead read only the first nrows

docs.title: Documentation style
docs.text:
Follow the PyEnsembl writing guide and the mhctools example.

Put installation and the first useful example on the home page. Give complete imports and concrete inputs, explain the result, and state prerequisites before the reader runs a command. Show output only when it has been checked. Label replaceable paths and templates.

Order guides by common tasks before advanced setup and implementation details. Keep desktop sidebar groups expanded initially and individually collapsible. Split a page when a substantial task or reference needs its own explanation. Preserve useful old links and anchors when moving content.

Use ordinary text for concepts and library names; reserve inline code for literal commands, API names, parameters, paths and values. Keep qualifications, experimental status and scientific limitations beside the claims they qualify.

Use system fonts, a readable line length and restrained headings. Let wide tables and code blocks scroll inside their containers. Avoid repetitive navigation lists in prose and excessive callouts.

Install requirements-docs.txt and run ./docs.sh before opening a PR. Review the home page and a reference page at desktop and narrow widths. Run the repository's required lint and test commands and execute complete examples. Documentation dependencies are separate from runtime dependencies.

docs.title: N-gram features
docs.text: PeptideVectorizer fits a vocabulary of residue n-grams, then transforms new sequences using that vocabulary. max_ngram controls the largest n-gram; normalize_row selects count normalization. Fit before calling transform(). These are sequence features, not binding predictions.

docs.title: Load assay data
docs.text:
These templates require network access on the first use and can download large IEDB exports. Review the loader's actual filters before interpreting a subset:

from pepdata.iedb import mhc, tcell

binding_assays = mhc.load_dataframe()
tcell_assays = tcell.load_dataframe()

The MHC-binding and T-cell tables represent different assays. A positive binding measurement is not automatically a positive T-cell response. Preserve assay, species and allele metadata when selecting records; the IEDB is the upstream data source.

Each module exposes download(force=False) and local_path(auto_download=True). Use those explicit acquisition interfaces when preparing an environment before loading a table. force=True requests a refresh; a cached export is a snapshot and does not by itself identify a pinned IEDB release.

See the loader reference for filtering arguments.

docs.title: Read a single-residue property
docs.text:
from pepdata.amino_acid_properties import hydropathy, volume

print(hydropathy["A"])
print(volume["A"])

1.8
91.5

Each table is a dictionary. Keep the scale and source context with the values when using them as features; the numbers from different properties are not interchangeable measurements.

docs.title: Read a pairwise coefficient
docs.text:
from pepdata.blosum import blosum62_dict

print(blosum62_dict["A"]["A"])

4

The first and second keys select the two residue letters. BLOSUM tables and the other pairwise matrices describe different quantities; consult the shipped matrix and its original source before interpreting coefficients.

docs.title: Use alphabets explicitly
docs.text: canonical_amino_acid_letters describes the standard residue alphabet. Extended and reduced alphabets are separate interfaces: do not assume every ambiguous letter has a value in every property table. Select and document an encoding policy before processing ambiguous sequences.
